subject: Dedicated deployment: traffic profile -> GPU mapping (initial intake)
messages:
From: Helen Lopez <helen.lopez@acme.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: ops-team@acme.com
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 22:12:00 +0000
Subject: Redwood Dedicated - workload profile and sizing kickoff

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for taking this -- we're evaluating a Dedicated deployment for Acme's customer support assistant. Before we set a call, here's a quick snapshot of what we think matters for sizing: 

- Baseline average QPS: 45 requests/sec (steady during business hours).
- Peak QPS: 420 requests/sec (minute-level spikes during promo events, ~2 hours/day).
- Typical concurrency per model replica: 6-12 concurrent requests depending on batching config.
- Prompt size (median): 120 tokens. Prompt size (90th): 420 tokens.
- Response size (median): 320 tokens. Response size (95th): 1,100 tokens.
- Percent of short queries (<50 tokens response): ~22%. Long generative sessions (multi-turn, >800 tokens total response): ~8% of requests.
- Preferred model family: open LLMs we can host (high-quality 70B family, but open to quantized 33B if cost-effective).
- Latency SLO: p95 end-to-end generation < 900ms for short responses, acceptable up to 3s for long ones during peaks.
- Budget note: looking to optimize $/1M tokens but not at the cost of severe latency regressions.

I've attached a small CSV with per-hour QPS from the last 14 days (acme_workload_snapshot.csv). Can you confirm what additional fields you need to produce a preliminary GPU mapping (node counts, recommended GPU type, expected autoscale headroom)?

If it's helpful, we can also share a 30-minute trace export.

Thanks,
Helen
Helen Lopez
Head of Ops, Acme Retail
helen.lopez@acme.com

Attachment: acme_workload_snapshot.csv (CSV, ~120KB)
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Helen Lopez <helen.lopez@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Jul 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood Dedicated - workload profile and sizing kickoff

Hi Helen -- thanks for the snapshot, this is very helpful. We've pulled the CSV and will triage it today. A few clarifying items that help us produce a tighter GPU map: 

1) Request mix: can you estimate percent split between single-shot prompts (one request -> one response) vs. multi-turn sessions that keep the KV cache warm? Multi-turn patterns let us assume better KV reuse and reduce per-token compute.
2) Peak shape: are the 420 QPS spikes sustained (minutes) or very short (few seconds)? We use different autoscale headroom for bursty spikes vs plateaued peaks.
3) Acceptable batching latency: if we recommend batching to lower $/token, what is the max added latency you can tolerate at p95 for short responses? (e.g., 50ms, 100ms, 200ms)
4) Model variant & quantization: is the acceptance for int8/4 quantized variants OK for non-critical features? Any regulatory constraints on quantization?
5) SLOs vs backlog: do you want guaranteed capacity (reserved headroom) or prefer aggressive autoscale with fallbacks to smaller models during rare saturation?

I'll attach our lightweight Dedicated sizing template to collect these details and some sample traces (redwood_dedicated_sizing_template.xlsx). If you prefer, we can schedule a 40-minute technical deep-dive where Marissa (solutions) and Dev (runtime) join to map traffic to a provisional fleet. Please let me know availability tomorrow afternoon (PDT).

Best,
Priyom Das
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood_dedicated_sizing_template.xlsx (Excel workbook)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Helen Lopez <helen.lopez@acme.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Jul 2026 10:35:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Redwood Dedicated - workload profile and sizing kickoff

Hi Helen -- copying a few quick, preliminary recommendations from a sizing lens before the deep-dive: 

- GPU family: for unquantized 70B-style models we typically recommend H100 or equivalent (memory + compute headroom). For int8/int4 quantized 70B equivalents, an H100 or A100-80GB with optimized kernels may work.
- Baseline estimate: to cover ~45 QPS steady with median response ~320 tokens, and latency SLOs without aggressive batching, we estimate ~6-10 H100-equipped replicas (this assumes per-replica concurrency tuned to 8 and prefix/KV caching for multi-turn).
- Peak/autoscale: to get to the 420 QPS peak safely with headroom for bursty minutes, plan for autoscale up to ~28 H100 replicas. If you adopt a quantized 33B as the primary inference model for majority of traffic and reserve 70B for long-tail, the peak node count can drop ~45-55%.
- Cost/time tradeoffs: quantization + sharded KV caching reduces both memory footprint and token cost; expect ~30-50% reduction in required GPU hours depending on accuracy tolerance.
- Quick ops ask: share a single-day sample trace with per-request latencies and token counts so Dev can run a micro-simulator on our side. A CSV with timestamp, prompt_tokens, response_tokens, latency_ms is enough.

We can walk these numbers through in the deep-dive. Priyom -- if Helen is ok, how about Thu Jul 3 at 16:00 UTC for a 40-minute slot?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
From: Helen Lopez <helen.lopez@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 03 Jul 2026 17:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Redwood Dedicated - workload profile and sizing kickoff

Marissa / Priyom -- that plan sounds good. We can provide the single-day trace and a 7-day sampler; attaching a zipped export (sample_trace_202606.zip). Peak spikes are typically minute-level (bursty) around regional promotions. We're comfortable trying an int8 quantized 33B as primary for 70% of traffic with the 70B variant held for sessions that require higher fidelity.

Confirming the deep-dive: Thu Jul 3 at 16:00 UTC works for our engineering lead (Sam Park). Calendar invite sent (see link). We'll also provide a short note on compliance constraints (no on-disk storage of tokens outside encrypted S3).

Best,
Helen
